mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the next 20 trading days signals monetary easing, reducing discount rates applied to equity cash flows and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 2.0% from a lower level triggers concerns about economic growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in tightening periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the rate remains above 2.0% for more than 60 days without returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained quarterly increase in GDP (GDPC1) over the next 20 trading days reflects growing economic demand, which enhances corporate profits and equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in expanding periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and sustained growth in GDP (GDPC1) over the next 20 trading days creates a favorable monetary and demand environment, amplifying equity valuations and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when proxies do not move in expected directions simultaneously (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) and industrial production (INDPRO) over the next 60 trading days signals labor market strength and supply chain expansion, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns not significantly higher than baseline when proxies do not move in expected directions simultaneously (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the next 20 trading days signals a soft landing, reducing inflationary pressures and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns not significantly positive in late-cycle expansion periods (t-test p > 0.05) or FEDFUNDS does not decline as expected.

mechanism_narrative: During a post-shock recovery regime (characterized by rising UNRATE and falling FEDFUNDS), a sustained increase in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) over the next 60 trading days signals labor market stabilization, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns not significantly positive when proxies do not move in expected directions during the regime (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden quarterly surge in GDP (GDPC1) over the next 5 trading days signals unexpected economic momentum, leading to short-term equity price appreciation and positive S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns not significantly positive when GDP does not surge unexpectedly (t-test p > 0.05).
